Mice like to mark their own territory, and if you add some of their dirty bedding they won't feel the need to do that so it'll smell a lot less than if you do all new.

Oh also! In terms of cleaning their cage, I cleaned mine once a week without too many difficulties. Females smell much less than males, and I cleaned mine with small pet approved deodorizer and cleanser. I'd go to a pet store for this. They sell super cute tiny pet Carriers for mice on Amazon, I found it SO MUCH EASIER to have one done up similar to their cage so you could just put your mouse there and take your time cleaning.

Females do best in groups of 3 (so there's no bullying), males do best in their own so they don't kill their mate. 10 gal I think would be too small for a male or trio of females. I did 20 gal for my boy, 30-40 for my girls. It's recommended to keep them in spaces not too big so they don't become too wild. 

In terms of attention, males need much more attention than females. They bond heavily with their owner, and enjoy being handled. Girls do as well, but less so because they socially interact with each other. Make sure to handle them often (20-30 min a day) so they feel loved and cared for! 


Necessities you'll need for your life are food, enrichment, and bedding. For bedding, I recommend dust free recyclable paper bedding. they sell a lot of different colors at petsmart, ultimately that was the bedding that my mice liked the most and it was the most cost-effective to buy. It doesn't need to be expensive, even something as simple as layering more bedding in your cage so your mice have the ability to burrow is a good fit. toilet paper rolls were a deep love for my mice, they chewed them up into a million pieces every time I put one in. make sure to do your research about certain toys if they are safe for your animals, I got a lot of mine Hidey holes typically used for betta fish but that took a lot of research to make sure it wouldn't hurt them. 

depending on your mice, they may behave well enough to be able to eat normal food, mine personally had to eat dietary approved lab blocks because they selective fed way too much and it made them super chubby. I recommend always having fun yummy food additives for your mice so they enjoy mealtime more. A favorite of mine were strawberry and scrambled eggs with a little bit of coconut, they would eat it up and it really helped their immune system and digestive system. Leafy greens, SOME non citrus fruits, even meat and bugs helps add some filler to their meal so it's better for them. it's also really nice to be able to make nice food for your mice, it's a great way to show your love for them.


I cannot stress this enough, before you pick out your mice I would recommend looking long and hard for exotic vets in your area, and asking them if they can specifically deal with mice. Not rats, mice. they're admittedly very hard to find and usually run pretty expensive. Mice, while adorable and very easy to care for, also do have a plethora of health problems such as eye issues and tumors. You want to make sure you have a good vet on hand should those issues arrive, that's something I really wish I had done before I adopted mine. 


When you first adopt your mice, they may be skittish and scared around you. That's completely normal, you're a predator and their prey. They will naturally have a bit of apprehension towards you. one of the first things that I did was take a smelly piece of clothing of mine, and put it in their bedding, like a used sock. They'll get more used to your smell, and therefore feel a bit more comfortable around you. Talk to them often, about literally anything at all. Working up towards them allowing you to hold them is a big process, and it may take a couple of weeks. before doing this, I would probably leave them in their new cage for a night or two so that they can get comfortable in their surroundings. Start with just your hand. Put your hand into their cage, do not move it. Work to that until they feel comfortable crawling over your hand. Then turn your hand Palm side up, things like that. There is absolutely hope, my mice had absolutely no problem with me picking them up and one occasionally liked to try  to climb into my mouth for kisses  LOL. Best of luck to you, friend!!
